paragraphs: The 530d has been a mainstay of the 5 Series diesel range since 2010, spanning two generations under one badge. F10/F11 cars (2010–2017) use the N57 — a 3.0-litre inline-six diesel that powered a wide range of BMW models of that era. From 2017, the G30/G31-generation 530d switched to the B57, a newer inline-six diesel that's a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the N57. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 530d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six diesel fitted to the 530d from 2010 to 2017. Known for turbo actuator wear over time — see the callout above. We inspect and replace turbo actuators, timing chain components and gaskets as standard on every N57 rebuild.
A 3.0-litre inline-six diesel fitted from 2017. Part of the later B-series engine family, which is generally reliable across the range, with no independently confirmed widespread defect pattern.

compatibility.intro: Because the 530d spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N57 part will work on a B57 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N57 or B57) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 530d quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
